audit_start_sha_role: clean F3 checkout before F4 test-quality corrections

claim_taxonomy.IMPLEMENTED: The implementation or interface exists in the inspected source tree.
claim_taxonomy.TESTED: A recorded automated test exercises the stated scope.
claim_taxonomy.VERIFIED: An internal invariant, analytical check or replay supports the stated scope.
claim_taxonomy.EXTERNALLY_VALIDATED: A comparable external oracle supports the stated observable and scope.
claim_taxonomy.QUALIFIED: A recorded decision accepts a bounded claim under its declared gate.
claim_taxonomy.EXPERIMENTAL: The path exists but is not accepted as a general qualified capability.

inventory.scan_policy: AST inventory plus targeted source and evidence review; test count is not used as a release-quality proxy.

assertions.interpretation: The two no-exception positive validators exercise APIs whose success contract is returning None; they are documented as a minor readability limitation, not a release blocker.

negative_testing.assessment: Existing negative tests cover the release-critical domains; F4 strengthens diagnostic specificity rather than adding duplicate cases.

existing_sensitive_regressions: MPI collective ordering and global readiness
explicit solver backend selection and no silent fallback
WEDGE6 fail-closed geometry and public maturity
F3 bounded public claims and link integrity

full_suite_result.assessment: The failures are in experimental or stale negative-path expectations outside the bounded public release matrix. They were not skipped, suppressed or converted to PASS; no F4 release blocker or supported-route regression was found.

determinism.assessment: Inspected random generators use explicit seeds; time, network and ordering-sensitive paths are either absent or controlled.

isolation.assessment: Temporary files use pytest-managed paths or explicit cleanup; environment mutation is fixture-scoped; no shared registry mutation was found in the inspected tests.

skip_policy.policy: No xfail is used to hide an unresolved failure. Optional skips are environment or evidence-policy gates and are not converted into PASS.

significant_skips.reason: External tools are optional and claims remain bounded by recorded evidence.
Live distributed execution is environment-dependent; fake adapters and contracts remain covered.
significant_skips.release_impact: Non-blocking for the default SciPy path; bounded PETSc evidence is separate.

significant_skips.reason: The dependency is optional and unavailable behavior is tested explicitly.
significant_skips.release_impact: Non-blocking; no Gmsh claim is inferred when skipped.

significant_skips.reason: Heavy or generated evidence is excluded from ordinary unit runs.
significant_skips.release_impact: Historical controlled evidence and governance records remain authoritative.

behavior_matrix.gap: Optional live PETSc/MPI paths are environment-gated.
HEX8R, SRI, B-bar and hourglass production routes remain deferred/research-only.
Static maturity is not promoted by modal evidence.
No transfer to static, general dynamics or other elements.
The registry, not a generic route label, defines the public boundary.
Finite-kinematic and postbuckling breadth remain limited.
No transfer of static/J2 maturity to contact.

behavior_matrix.surface: reactions, energy, BCs, loads and materials
behavior_matrix.gap: External comparison is only claimed when comparable.

behavior_matrix.surface: API, CLI, packaging, registry and preflight
behavior_matrix.gap: Optional live external environments are not part of default CI.

mutation_analysis.mutation: change the sign of an element stiffness contribution
drop a local element contribution during assembly
route a request to the wrong backend

findings.title: Critical negative tests caught any Exception rather than the contract category.
findings.scope: 17 pytest.raises sites across backend, schema, Gmsh, PETSc, solver and WEDGE6 tests.
findings.correction: Assertions now use the concrete InputValidationError, MeshValidationError, InfrastructureError, NumericalConvergenceError, ValueError or RuntimeError contract as applicable.

findings.title: Optional live PETSc/MPI, Gmsh and external-oracle execution is environment-gated in ordinary test runs.
findings.correction: No skip was removed or converted into PASS; contract tests and controlled evidence remain the release basis.
findings.follow_up: Exercise live optional environments in their dedicated qualification jobs.

findings.title: The full suite retains three pre-existing failures in experimental or stale nonlinear test paths.
findings.scope: Finite-sliding contact, geometric-nonlinear invalid-load expectation and finite-sliding benchmark tests.
findings.evidence: The failures occur before the claimed release-supported bounded route can execute: the fail-closed preflight rejects an unsupported discrete/nonlinear combination, and one negative test uses an object load that is rejected before its older message assertion.
findings.correction: No skip, xfail or expectation weakening was added. The failures remain visible for a later experimental-route/test-contract decision.
findings.release_impact: Non-blocking for the documented 0.2.7 supported/bounded matrix; no P0/P1 release claim depends on these paths.

findings.title: Cached elasticity matrix identity assertion was opaque.
findings.correction: The test now names both reads and also asserts the expected matrix shape.

findings.title: Two validator success tests rely on the no-exception success contract.
findings.reason: The validators return None on success; adding a redundant assertion would not strengthen behavior.

findings.title: No mutation-testing framework or global coverage campaign was added.
findings.reason: The requested mutation-style analysis was performed against critical behaviors; a framework would add release tooling rather than targeted confidence here.

validation.full_test_suite: 2142 passed, 3 failed, 184 skipped, 2 warnings in 1577.06s; three failures deferred as pre-existing experimental/stale paths

conclusion.answer_to_release_question: For officially supported and bounded routes, the suite provides reasonable pre-publication regression confidence because critical results, invariants, dispatch, invalid-input behavior and release guards are asserted. The full-suite audit retains three visible failures in experimental or stale nonlinear paths; they are not evidence against the supported release matrix, but those paths are not release-ready.
limitations: Live optional PETSc/MPI, Gmsh and external environments remain separately gated.
A small number of validator success tests express success through absence of an exception because the API returns None.
Three pre-existing full-suite failures remain in experimental or stale finite-sliding/geometric-nonlinear test expectations; no skip or xfail was added.
No heavy benchmark or global coverage/mutation campaign is part of F4.
